_note: Hand-authored content for the fictional universe (Scout v0). Every name here is invented. Any resemblance to real clubs, places or people is coincidental.
country_note: Meridia is a fictional football nation. Its towns, clubs and people are invented.

clubs.name: Brackwater Athletic
clubs.summary: A harbour-town club founded by lamp-factory workers, famous for its loud North stand and a youth academy that feeds the first team.
clubs.crest: A navy shield with an amber street lamp at its centre and a harbour chain across the bottom. Four small chimneys above the shield recall the Harrow Quay lamp factory, and a ribbon below carries the motto 'Lux in Portu' (light in the harbour).

clubs.name: Calderholm United
clubs.summary: Born in the pottery district across the estuary from Brackwater, Calderholm play a direct, high-pressing game and have won the league four times.
clubs.crest: A maroon roundel with a white bottle kiln at its centre and two crossed potter's paddles beneath it, inside a sky-blue ring that reads 'Calderholm United 1894'.

clubs.name: Fennmoor Town
clubs.summary: A marshland club known for patient passing and the heron painted on the roof of its main stand.
clubs.crest: A dark green shield with a white heron standing on one leg among marsh reeds, and a thin white border.

clubs.name: Port Ellery FC
clubs.summary: The oldest club in Meridia, three-time champions, with a ground built right against the sea wall.
clubs.crest: An off-white roundel with a teal sea wall and three breaking waves, ringed in teal with 'Port Ellery FC 1887'.

clubs.name: Ravensgate City
clubs.summary: The capital's biggest club and current champions, with the largest budget in the league.
clubs.crest: A black shield with a silver raven, wings spread, perched on a city gate, under a small silver crown for the capital.

clubs.name: Ostwick Albion
clubs.summary: A textile-town club from the capital's east side, proud of a stand built by its own supporters in 1951.
clubs.crest: A red shield crossed by a white weaving shuttle, with a white thread looping around it into a knot.

clubs.name: Marrowdale Wanderers
clubs.summary: A valley club that once played on a cattle market; tangerine shirts and a reputation for late goals.
clubs.crest: A tangerine shield with a black drover's crook and a bull's head above a narrow valley, edged in black.

clubs.name: Saltrigg Rangers
clubs.summary: Founded by salt miners; the club song is still sung before every home game.
clubs.crest: A royal blue roundel with two crossed white pickaxes over a pile of salt crystals, ringed in white.

clubs.name: Glenvarra FC
clubs.summary: The highest ground in Meridia, where visiting teams complain about the wind.
clubs.crest: A purple shield with a gold stag's head and antlers in front of three mountain peaks.

clubs.name: Westmere Harriers
clubs.summary: A club that began as an athletics society; its players still train on the old running track.
clubs.crest: A yellow shield with a navy lark in flight over an oval running track drawn in navy.

clubs.name: Kingsfold Rovers
clubs.summary: Riverside club with a famous academy and a habit of selling its best young players.
clubs.crest: A blue roundel with an orange kingfisher diving into a wavy river, ringed in orange.

clubs.name: Ellesby Town
clubs.summary: A cathedral-town club; the bells ring after every home win.
clubs.crest: A claret shield with a cream cathedral bell, with two smaller bells above it on either side.

clubs.name: Alder Cross FC
clubs.summary: A railway-junction club promoted two seasons ago and fighting to stay up.
clubs.crest: A green shield with two gold railway lines crossing in an X, and an alder leaf above the junction.

clubs.name: Hollin Vale United
clubs.summary: Twice cup winners in the last five years, known for a strong defence.
clubs.crest: A white shield split by a black chevron for the valley, with a black holly leaf in the lower half.

clubs.name: Copperhythe FC
clubs.summary: One of the smallest grounds in the top division, and the loudest atmosphere per seat, according to its fans.
clubs.crest: A copper-coloured shield with a black anvil and a crossed hammer and tongs, edged in black.

clubs.name: Wexmouth Town
clubs.summary: A seaside club with sky-blue shirts and a long cup tradition.
clubs.crest: A sky-blue roundel with a white gull gliding over a lighthouse, ringed in white with 'Wexmouth Town'.

clubs.name: Lowmarsh FC
clubs.summary: Newly promoted, playing in the top division for the first time in 31 years.
clubs.crest: An olive green shield with white reeds rising from three wavy white lines of water.

clubs.name: Tarnhaven Rovers
clubs.summary: A lake-district club with slate-grey shirts and a red sash.
clubs.crest: A slate-grey shield with a red diagonal sash and a small white lake with a boat in the upper corner.

clubs.name: Pellam Forest FC
clubs.summary: Relegated last season and favourites to bounce straight back.
clubs.crest: A forest green shield with a gold woodsman's axe across a gold pine tree.

clubs.name: Quarrington Town
clubs.summary: A quarry-town club whose stands are built from local stone.
clubs.crest: A stone-grey shield built of blue-outlined blocks like a wall, with a blue quarry hammer at the centre.

clubs.name: Brennock City
clubs.summary: A mill-town club with a famous scarf-twirling tradition at kick-off.
clubs.crest: A teal roundel with a white windmill, its four sails forming an X, ringed in white.

clubs.name: Dunstrow Athletic
clubs.summary: A farming-town club with one of the oldest wooden stands in the country.
clubs.crest: A white shield with a green shepherd's crook and a green sheep below it, on a green hillside base.

clubs.name: Skelmoor Albion
clubs.summary: Purple-shirted moorland club, cup semi-finalists two seasons ago.
clubs.crest: A purple shield with a white moorland grouse and white heather sprigs at its feet.

clubs.name: Vanbridge United
clubs.summary: Named after the iron bridge in the town centre, painted orange every summer by fans.
clubs.crest: A burnt orange shield with a white iron bridge of three arches across the middle.

clubs.name: Hewlett Green FC
clubs.summary: A village club that climbed five divisions in twenty years.
clubs.crest: A green roundel with a black village green and a black maypole, and five black stars for the five divisions climbed.

clubs.name: Oakhurst Town
clubs.summary: Brown-and-gold shirts, and an oak tree planted behind the goal for every promotion.
clubs.crest: A brown shield with a gold acorn hanging from a gold oak leaf.

clubs.name: Mirefield Rovers
clubs.summary: A canal-town club whose fans arrive by boat for the derby.
clubs.crest: An indigo shield with a light grey canal narrowboat on wavy lines, under a grey lock gate.

clubs.name: Crowhill FC
clubs.summary: Black-and-yellow hill-town club with a famously steep terrace.
clubs.crest: A black shield with a yellow crow perched on the top of a steep yellow hill.

clubs.name: Embersley Borough
clubs.summary: Smallest professional club in Meridia, run partly by volunteers.
clubs.crest: A charcoal shield with three burnt-orange flames rising from a bed of glowing embers.

clubs.name: Falconridge City
clubs.summary: Ambitious club with a new training centre and promotion as the stated goal.
clubs.crest: A dark slate shield with a light blue falcon diving, wings folded, over a mountain ridge.

clubs.name: Stonewick Rangers
clubs.summary: Promoted last season; a granite-quarry town whose fans carry chisels painted in club colours.
clubs.crest: A grey shield with a red stonemason's chisel and mallet crossed over a granite block.

clubs.name: Brindlemoor Athletic
clubs.summary: Back in the top division after a long absence, built on a thrifty scouting network.
clubs.crest: A green roundel with a white moorhen walking on a white reed bed, ringed in white.

clubs.name: Quillhaven Town
clubs.summary: Old printing town with a loyal crowd and a famous blue-and-yellow scarf wall.
clubs.crest: A navy shield with a yellow quill pen crossing an open yellow book.

clubs.name: Tidewell FC
clubs.summary: Seaside club whose ground floods spray onto the away end on stormy days.
clubs.crest: A teal roundel with a single white breaking wave filling the lower half, ringed in white.

clubs.name: Larkspur Rovers
clubs.summary: Small country club known for its open-air family atmosphere.
clubs.crest: A purple shield with a lilac lark on a sprig of lilac larkspur flowers.

clubs.name: Wrenfield Athletic
clubs.summary: Mill-town club that relies on a busy youth academy.
clubs.crest: A brown shield with a cream wren perched on a cream mill wheel.

clubs.name: Greywater Albion
clubs.summary: Relegated last season and determined to bounce straight back.
clubs.crest: A blue-grey shield with a white grebe swimming on wavy white lines.

clubs.name: Ironmoss City
clubs.summary: Former steel town with a gritty, physical style of play.
clubs.crest: A black shield with an orange smelting furnace pouring a stream of molten iron into a ladle.

clubs.name: Cobbleford Town
clubs.summary: One of the oldest clubs in Meridia, playing in a tight ground in the old market square.
clubs.crest: A red shield with a white market cross standing on a base of white cobblestones.

clubs.name: Hollowmere United
clubs.summary: Lakeside club whose supporters arrive by rowing boat for the season opener.
clubs.crest: A royal blue roundel with a light blue otter swimming across a lake, ringed in light blue.

clubs.name: Pennerby FC
clubs.summary: The newest club in the second division, promoted twice in four seasons.
clubs.crest: A gold shield with a black pennant flag on a black pole, the pennant carrying a small gold star.

clubs.name: Kestrel Vale
clubs.summary: Hill-valley club famous for winter matches played in thick fog.
clubs.crest: A dark brown shield with a peach kestrel hovering over a valley, wisps of fog drawn across its base.

clubs.name: Fernhollow FC
clubs.summary: Forest-town club with a wooden main stand dating from the 1920s.
clubs.crest: A deep green shield with a pale green fern frond curling from bottom to top.

clubs.name: Marrowby United
clubs.summary: Market-garden town club, proud of a pitch kept by volunteer groundskeepers.
clubs.crest: An olive shield with a white spade and a white watering can crossed beneath a marrow.

roll_of_honour_note: Winners since 2005/06 (club ids). The Super Shield is played in August at the start of the season (league champions v cup winners of the season before) and is labelled by year. Older titles of the two match clubs are in match_clubs.json.
